title: AI Safety and Guardrails Systems Check

questions.question: Why is an output classifier alone not a guardrails system?
options: Output classifiers cannot return confidence scores
It cannot independently constrain data access, tool authority, approvals, and incident response
Classifiers only work on images
A model cannot call application tools
questions.explanation: Guardrails are a system of independent boundaries. Content evaluation cannot replace authorization, least privilege, complete mediation, or operational response.

questions.question: An untrusted document asks an agent to export tenant records. Which control most directly limits the blast radius if the model follows the instruction?
options: A longer system prompt
A lower sampling temperature
A policy-enforcing tool gateway with least-privilege credentials
A larger context window
questions.explanation: Treat model output as untrusted. The downstream gateway must authorize every action and expose only the minimum capability.

questions.question: What should a high-impact write path do when its policy service is unavailable?
options: Proceed and log the decision later
Retry forever while holding the request open
Fail closed or fall back to a non-actioning mode
Let the model decide whether the action is safe
questions.explanation: Missing policy evidence must not silently become permission. A bounded fallback can still return information without changing external state.

questions.question: In the public support fixture, the balanced operating point has 92% recall over 400 unsafe cases. Approximately how many unsafe cases are missed?
questions.explanation: The miss rate is 8%. Multiplying 400 by 0.08 gives 32 false negatives.

questions.question: Why can a high-recall safety detector still block a release?
options: Recall is never useful
Its false-positive load can violate the safe-interruption or review-capacity gate
Every detector must have zero alerts
Release gates should use one average score
questions.explanation: Independent gates protect different harms. Strong recall does not cancel excessive interruption or an unserviceable review queue.

questions.question: Which fairness check is most likely to expose a regression hidden by a stable global average?
options: Model file size
Aggregate request volume
Outcome and intervention rates on protected and intersectional slices
Average prompt length
questions.explanation: Aggregate metrics can hide concentrated harm. Slice-level outcomes, errors, overrides, and appeals make disparities visible.

questions.question: Which evidence is necessary to reproduce why a request was allowed, blocked, or escalated?
options: Only the final model text
Only the user identifier
Versioned input, model, policy, tool, decision, and override records
A screenshot of the dashboard
questions.explanation: A replayable decision needs the complete versioned path, while privacy controls should minimize and protect retained data.
